title: Teltonika
desc: Industrial cellular routers, gateways and remote management

pages.t: Teltonika Networks is part of the Lithuanian Teltonika group, which is headquartered in Vilnius. It makes industrial cellular routers, gateways, switches and modems, plus a cloud tool called RMS to manage them.
g: Cellular router
A router that connects to the internet through a mobile network (4G or 5G) using a SIM card.
Gateway
A device that connects equipment, such as meters or sensors, to a network or the cloud.

pages.h: Built for places with no cable
pages.t: Many sites have no fixed internet: vehicles, pumps, kiosks, remote cabinets. Teltonika says its routers use 2G to 5G mobile networks with dual SIM, eSIM support and automatic failover. Exact features vary by model.
g: Dual SIM
Two SIM card slots, so the router can use a second operator if the first one fails.
Failover
Automatic switch to a backup connection when the main one goes down.
eSIM
A SIM built into the device, programmed remotely instead of a plastic card.

pages.t: Teltonika groups its use cases as industrial and automation, energy and utilities, smart city, transportation, enterprise and retail. Think machines, meters, buses, shops and backup lines.

quiz.q: What is Teltonika Networks best known for?
quiz.w: The company makes industrial cellular routers, gateways, switches and modems, plus the RMS management tool.

quiz.q: Which feature lets a router use a second mobile operator if the first fails?
quiz.w: Dual SIM means two SIM slots, and failover switches over automatically.
g: Dual SIM
Two SIM card slots, so the router can use a second operator if the first one fails.
Failover
Automatic switch to a backup connection when the main one goes down.

quiz.q: A customer needs internet for a remote pump station with no cable. Which kind of product fits?
quiz.w: Cellular routers use mobile networks, so no fixed line is needed.
g: Cellular router
A router that connects to the internet through a mobile network (4G or 5G) using a SIM card.

quiz.q: Which is NOT one of the sectors Teltonika lists for its use cases?
quiz.w: The listed sectors are industrial, energy, smart city, transportation, enterprise and retail.

lessons.title: The router series: RUT, RUTX, RUTM, RUTC

pages.t: The RUT range is the compact entry. RUT1 has no mobile modem at all, RUT2 is small cellular, and RUT9 is described as versatile industrial cellular with two SIM slots. Good for simple remote jobs.
g: Modem
The part that talks to the mobile network.

pages.t: RUTX and RUTM are both described by Teltonika as series of routers for advanced industrial solutions. Both have Gigabit Ethernet ports and two SIM slots, and both include 5G models, such as RUTX50 and RUTM50. Step up here for more ports and power.
g: Gigabit Ethernet
Wired network ports running at up to 1 Gbps, ten times faster than older 100 Mbps ports.

pages.t: RUTC is the most powerful of these four: more memory, Wi-Fi 6, five Gigabit ports and Docker support for running extra applications on the router itself.
g: Docker
A way to run small software packages on a device. Mostly a technician topic.

quiz.q: Which RUT model has no mobile modem?
quiz.w: RUT1 is described as a compact industrial router without a mobile connection.
g: Modem
The part that talks to the mobile network.

quiz.q: A customer wants to run extra applications on the router, with Wi-Fi 6. Which series fits?
quiz.w: RUTC adds Wi-Fi 6, more memory and Docker support.
g: Docker
A way to run small software packages on a device.

quiz.q: Which pair is described as routers for advanced industrial solutions?
quiz.w: Teltonika describes both RUTX and RUTM that way.

quiz.q: A simple remote kiosk needs a small, basic cellular router. Where do you start?
quiz.w: RUT2 is small cellular, RUT9 is versatile industrial cellular with two SIM slots.

pages.t: TRB gateways link equipment to the cloud over 4G, 5G, LTE-M or NB-IoT. They add industrial interfaces like RS232, RS485 and Modbus, so old machines and meters can be reached.
g: Old but common serial cable standards that industrial equipment still uses.
Modbus
A common language that industrial machines use to share readings.
LTE-M / NB-IoT
Low-power mobile networks for small devices that send little data.

pages.t: OTD routers are made for outdoor use. ATRM is built for transportation, with M12 connectors and railway certification. Altos are 5G Wi-Fi 7 routers aimed at fixed wireless access.
g: Fixed wireless access
Internet to a building over a mobile network instead of a cable.

pages.t: TSW are industrial switches and TSF are flat Ethernet switches. TAP are Wi-Fi access points, for example TAP200, a Wi-Fi 5 model for medium-density spaces such as retail or enterprise sites. DAP are industrial access points.
g: Switch
Connects wired devices in a local network.
Access point
Adds Wi-Fi to a wired network.

quiz.q: Which family connects serial industrial equipment to the cloud over mobile networks?
quiz.w: TRB gateways support RS232, RS485 and Modbus with 4G or 5G.
g: Old but common serial cable standards that industrial equipment still uses.

quiz.q: A customer needs a router outside in the weather. Which series is made for it?
quiz.w: OTD routers are designed for outdoor use.

quiz.q: Which product would you offer a shop that needs more Wi-Fi coverage?
quiz.w: TAP200 is a Wi-Fi 5 access point for medium-density spaces such as retail.
g: Access point
Adds Wi-Fi to a wired network.

quiz.q: Which series is built for trains and vehicles, with M12 connectors?
quiz.w: ATRM is built for transportation with M12 Ethernet and power connectors.

pages.t: RMS is Teltonika's Remote Management System. It lets you monitor devices and change their settings from the cloud, even when they have no public IP address. No site visit is needed.
g: Public IP address
An internet address that can be reached from outside. Many mobile connections do not give one.

pages.t: The manual lists modules: Management (devices, reports, alerts, tasks), RMS Connect for remote access, RMS VPN for secure links, and Administration for users and companies. There is also an API.
g: VPN
A private encrypted tunnel across the internet.
API
A way for other software to talk to a system automatically.

pages.h: Why it matters in a deal
pages.t: Checking status and changing settings on many routers from one place saves truck rolls. For a reseller it can turn a hardware sale into a managed service. Check the current RMS licence terms with Allnet before quoting.
g: Truck roll
A trip by a technician to a site, expensive when repeated.

quiz.q: What does RMS do?
o: Monitors and configures Teltonika devices from the cloud
quiz.w: RMS is a cloud tool for monitoring and managing Teltonika devices.

quiz.q: Which RMS module gives remote access to a device?
quiz.w: RMS Connect covers remote access, as the manual lists.

quiz.q: A reseller has 200 routers at remote sites. Why pitch RMS?
o: Update and monitor them all without site visits
quiz.w: Central monitoring, alerts and remote access save technician trips.
g: Truck roll
A trip by a technician to a site, expensive when repeated.

quiz.q: RMS can reach devices even without what?
quiz.w: The wiki says RMS works even if devices have no public IP.
g: Public IP address
An internet address that can be reached from outside. Many mobile connections do not give one.

pages.h: Match the site to the series
pages.t: Basic remote site or kiosk: RUT2 or RUT9. Need Gigabit ports or 5G: RUTM or RUTX. Heavy workloads and Wi-Fi 6: RUTC. Outdoors: OTD. Vehicles and rail: ATRM. Serial meters and machines: TRB (some RUT9 models too).

pages.h: Features that point to a series
pages.t: The wiki shows RS-232 or RS-485 serial ports on most RUT9 models, handy for meters. Many RUTX models add GNSS location, some also Bluetooth LE. OTD routers are weather-rated, with PoE on the Ethernet ports.
g: GNSS
Satellite positioning, like GPS, so a device can report where it is.
PoE
Power over Ethernet: power and data over one network cable.

pages.h: When it is not the whole answer
pages.t: For a full office network or deep security inspection, Teltonika is often only one part, and a firewall vendor may be needed too. If the job is mainly reading old serial equipment, look at TRB gateways before a router.
g: Firewall
A security gate that filters traffic between networks.

quiz.q: A bus operator wants a vehicle router with Wi-Fi and GNSS location. Which series is built for transportation?
quiz.w: ATRM is Teltonika's transportation series, with GNSS, Wi-Fi and M12 connectors.
g: GNSS
Satellite positioning, like GPS, so a device can report where it is.

quiz.q: A utility must read old meters over RS485 and send data by mobile. Best fit?
quiz.w: TRB gateways add serial interfaces and cellular links.
g: Old but common serial cable standards that industrial equipment still uses.

quiz.q: A water company wants a 5G router in an outdoor roadside cabinet. Which do you look at?
quiz.w: OTD is the outdoor series, and OTD500 is the 5G model.

quiz.q: A customer wants a router that runs extra apps and has Wi-Fi 6. Which?
quiz.w: RUTC has Wi-Fi 6 and Docker support.

pages.t: Teltonika products are the hardware that uses mobile broadband. The customer still needs a SIM and data plan from an operator. Ask early: which operator, how many SIMs, and is a backup SIM wanted?
g: Mobile broadband
Internet delivered over the 4G or 5G network.

pages.t: How many sites? What must it connect: Wi-Fi users, machines or meters? Indoors or outdoors? Is backup connectivity needed? Should it be managed centrally in RMS? The answers point to the right series.
Model lines change, and the wiki keeps an end-of-life category. Confirm current availability and which series fits with your Allnet contact. Do not promise a feature that is not on the datasheet.
g: End of life (EOL)
A product that is being or has been discontinued.

quiz.q: What does the customer still need besides a Teltonika cellular router?
quiz.w: The router uses an operator's mobile network, so a SIM and plan are required.

quiz.q: Which question helps pick between RUT, TRB and OTD?
o: What must it connect and where is it installed?
quiz.w: Use case and location point to the right series.

quiz.q: Where does the wiki list products being discontinued?
quiz.w: The wiki has a category for end-of-life products, so check before quoting.
g: End of life (EOL)
A product that is being or has been discontinued.

quiz.q: A shop wants a backup internet line for its main fibre. What do you discuss?
quiz.w: A router with a mobile connection can take over when the main line fails.
g: Failover
Automatic switch to a backup connection when the main one goes down.

about: Lithuanian maker of industrial cellular routers, gateways and switches, with a cloud tool called RMS to manage them remotely.
Targets industrial and automation, energy and utilities, smart city, transport, enterprise and retail: vehicles, pumps, kiosks and remote cabinets with no fixed internet.
Different because it is built for places without cable: mobile networks with dual SIM and automatic failover, and on some models serial ports for old meters and machines.
